Treatment summary
Patient presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with pain and swelling
of the left wrist. Physical examination demonstrated focal tenderness over the distal
radius, restricted range of motion, and reduced grip strength. Radiograhps conifrmed a
distal radius fracture, and the findings are clear and consistent with the mechanism
described, with the force of the impact being in keeping with this type of injury. The
patient has no known prior injury to this area. Management consisted of immobilization
in a splint, analgesia as needed, and a structured home exercise program once healing
allowed. Over four visits, the patient progressed steadily, with pain and swelling
decreasing and mobility improving, and visit frequency was reduced accordingly as
recovery advanced. Billed services reflect the expected sequence of care, with no
duplicated charges for the same treatment. Continued follow-up is planned to monitor
union and functional recovery.
